paper_source: OpenAI supplied 5 October 2026 preprint; local source.pdf SHA-256 a99f1c38d086a33591b6204ae3957fe3f25c8f31d97c48087325a18fd66daf3e; extracted.md source locators from intake and the cited returns.

reviews.rationale: The equivalence R f ≤ t ↔ RLe f t, together with Statement.lean RLe and finite positive tree mixture, expresses the attained worst-case randomized minimum; read-all proves feasibility.

QLe and AdaptiveProgram specify input-independent programs, unitary and projective steps, syntactic branch cap, oracle, and promised-input 2/3 success; the equivalence gives the attained minimum. The special constant branch covers empty query registers.
DLe and QueryTree specify exact evaluation on the promise and worst-case tree depth; the equivalence expresses the attained minimum, and applies in particular to total f.
The declaration conjoins basis XOR action, involution and a complex-linear isometry for the same oracle.
The infimum is over nonnegative real exponents, a finite real constant, every n≥1 and every total f; the positive-constant presentation is proved equivalent.

premises: Fixed k ≥ 2; sufficiently large m=4^t.
reviews.rationale: For fixed k the theorem gives positive constants and exponent, a threshold, and the same realizing circuit for the quantum and randomized inequalities; the extra circuit-size witness strengthens the row.
This proves only alphaTot=4. It does not itself conjoin the universal bound and family clause, so the whole-row relation is partial.
The theorem states alphaTot=4 with an explicit BansalSinhaLower binder and omits the other row clauses; later discharge elsewhere does not remove this binder.
The BansalSinhaLower binder is open in this declaration and the family conclusion still contains pointwise 8≤t and L<R(P) implications; this is not the unconditional whole-row statement.

Its conjunction contains alphaTot=4, UniversalPower 4 and, for each fixed k≥2, one threshold and realizing-circuit family with quantum bound and strict floor lower bound. The conversion of floors to the equation (2) asymptotic is in ConstructionFamily. The Forrelation and quartic implementations use alternative routes.
The full no-cubic-bound conclusion has the explicit BansalSinhaLower binder; the binder remains open in this declaration.
The conclusion denies one constant bounding R by C Q³ uniformly over every n≥1 and every total function; no mathematical binder remains.

premises: Two winning columns on the same input.
reviews.rationale: The theorem asserts equality of winning columns for arbitrary circuits and partial functions, extending the paper construction.

premises: W is the sum of weights and W>0; comparison table is complementary with zero diagonal.
reviews.rationale: The conjunction gives both algebraic equalities and the half-weight inequality, for arbitrary real weights. Nonnegativity is required when interpreting these weights as a probability law, not for the displayed algebra.
The theorem conjoins R≤D and D≤20736(1+Q)^4 uniformly, via complexitylib; the coefficient is not 1500625 or 19600.

The type itself is the one-plus bound with coefficient 1500625 and R≤D. A separate source theorem gives the stronger no-plus D≤1500625 Q^4. This route uses the Appendix A suppliers, with alternative Huang multiplicity proof.
Both half-dimensions are present for d>0. Square, trace and eigenvalue classification are separate declarations; this one remains partial against the compound corrected row.
The theorem gives one realizing circuit and an explicit O_k(m log²m) bound, for a wider k range than the paper row.
It conjoins the Phi² law and promise gaps with k logical reads and a Runs (2*k) physical witness. It does not provide an end-to-end Runs k witness; local phase kickback alone does not close that gap.
The declaration gives an accurate Boolean isometry, physical continuation retaining the embedded state and all-input normalized output law; the 2nk physical cap remains within O_k(1+log(1/η)).

premises: Nonnegative normalized prior; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: Only E Z≤4G/m is stated, derived from the coefficient-two finite-world induction. The canonical row also asserts early and late subclaims, which are absent.

premises: Nonnegative address weights.
reviews.rationale: The type proves the absolute coupling bound without a depth cap. The current canonical row already has an absolute gap, whereas the cited preprint display is one-sided; the stronger relation here refers to dropping the depth cap.

premises: 1≤L; normalized nonnegative promise-supported prior; one-instance hardness at L; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: The absolute gap implies the one-sided canonical conclusion; the coefficient-four statement is derived through the alternative coefficient-two erased-zero estimate.

premises: C realizes f; 1≤L≤m; L<R(f).
reviews.rationale: For every finite partial-function input type it proves the strict floor lower bound for the corresponding addressed construction. The f-hardness condition is part of the target proposition, not an extra open assumption.

premises: Fixed k≥2; C realizes P.
reviews.rationale: One k-dependent threshold works for every realizing circuit; the strict G floor result is unconditional in this declaration and stronger than a single selected circuit.

premises: W is the sum of weights and W>0; comparison table is complementary with zero diagonal.
reviews.rationale: Comparator tournament identity only: the half-weight inequality is not part of this declaration.

premises: W is the sum of weights and W>0; comparison table is complementary with zero diagonal.
reviews.rationale: Comparator tournament inequality only: the displayed equality chain is not part of this declaration.

premises: Two WinsAt witnesses for the same input.
reviews.rationale: Comparator construction theorem proves equality of both the winning column and its address; winner witnesses give the column-only corollary.

premises: Fixed address data A; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: The bound is 2G/m² averaged over independent uniform zero positions and I, but the type omits the equality to expectedZeros/m and uses fixed address data.

The exact equality between hit weighted average and expectedZeros/m holds algebraically for arbitrary real μ; probability interpretation additionally uses a normalized nonnegative law. The bound clause is absent.

premises: Nonnegative normalized address-data distribution; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: The declaration proves the coefficient-four hit-probability upper bound but does not itself include the displayed equality.

premises: Nonnegative normalized address-data distribution; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: This single type states hit probability = E Z/m and E Z/m ≤ 4G/m², with m=2^ℓ, extending the paper’s m=4^t. The bound uses finite-world induction rather than the printed early/late argument.

premises: Nonnegative normalized address-data distribution; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: This single type states hit probability = E Z/m and hit probability ≤ 4G/m²; equality turns the second clause into the displayed chained bound. It allows m=2^ℓ, and uses the alternative finite-world bound.

premises: Nonnegative normalized address-data distribution; tree depth≤G.
reviews.rationale: The independently specified product-law hitProbability and expectedCount state the complete equality and bound for m=2^ℓ; the bridge maps the explicitly defined dummy experiment and distinct-discovery count to the maintained formulation. It still shares coordinate, tree, path and depth interfaces.

premises: m = 4^t; arbitrary k sign strings.
reviews.rationale: Conjoins bit signs, Walsh parity entries, normalized H, uniform u and sign diagonals. Statement.lean mValue=2^(2t), walshSign and forrelation definitions, and construction_forr_sqrt_mValue make the interpretation exact.
The alternating word has k sign diagonals and k−1 H factors; the statement includes δ=2^(−5k). Paper fixes k≥2, so the explicit k≥1 premise covers its domain.
The cardinality, true, false and undefined cases and disjointness appear together; P is implemented by the integer tests, proved equivalent here.

The corrected row is the definition of L only; the old uncorrected intake row also included the randomized inequality. Nat.floor agrees with ordinary floor here for the paper’s k≥2 and sufficiently large m, where the argument is nonnegative.

premises: Fixed k ≥ 2; arbitrary c > 0; sufficiently large t with m=4^t.
reviews.rationale: The corrected row chooses the positive literature constant c; this theorem works for every c>0. It is only numerical comparison, not a proof of the cited Bansal–Sinha bound. Base-two logarithms differ by an absorbed positive constant from another fixed base.

premises: Fixed k ≥ 2; arbitrary c > 0; sufficiently large t with m=4^t.
reviews.rationale: In addition to the strict comparison it gives the unfloored middle term. It does not assert an external lower bound.

Statement.lean BansalSinhaLower unfolds to ∀ k≥2, ∃ t₀, ∀ t≥t₀, Lvalue k t < R(P k t). The theorem proves this proposition without a BansalSinhaLower hypothesis; its proof is the local alternative lower-bound route rather than the preprint’s citation.
The integer numerator is the matrix word with the first diagonal absorbed by the ones vector; the theorem also states Φ=N/M, positive M=m(√m)^(k−1), W=√m H and ±1 entries.
Both numerical equivalences plus promised/true predicates are stated; the actual circuit bits d and b required in the row are absent from this declaration.

premises: k=l+1; arbitrary input and a gate-consistent transcript.
reviews.rationale: The actual circuit value bit equals the first comparison and its domain bit the disjunction; the equivalences of the real-valued Φ tests are in another declaration. A consistent transcript is ordinary circuit semantics.

premises: Fixed k≥2; m=4^t; lower bound eventually in t and circuit asymptotic from t≥1.
reviews.rationale: One conjunction gives the eventually valid R bound; one retained-state coherent physical witness, accuracy and all-input output law with fixed-k logarithmic budget; and a uniformly bounded realizing circuit. The local proof of part (i) is alternative to the cited route.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: The type characterizes degree through Fourier support; it does not alone assert the row’s unique multilinear polynomial, constant-zero convention and input/output sign equivalences. Adjacent degree_const and degree_eq_sign are distinct declarations.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: The type fixes the supremum over inputs and families. The nonempty block and flipping semantics are separately given by appendixA_isSensitiveBlock_iff and the imported family definition.

premises: Input-indexed real matrix and coordinate i.
reviews.rationale: It states the entry mask exactly; the row also specifies the Euclidean operator-norm convention, a separate definition appendixAMatrixNorm.

premises: Γ real, symmetric and entrywise nonnegative.
reviews.rationale: AppendixAPerronWitness expands to coordinatewise nonnegative v, sum v²=1, and Γv=‖Γ‖v, with the Euclidean operator norm. Γ need not be nonzero; the input cube is nonempty even for n=0.

premises: Finite workspace W; arbitrary input-indexed state family Ψ.
reviews.rationale: Its body is the complex weighted sum vₓvᵧΓₓᵧ⟨Ψₓ,Ψᵧ⟩; substitution of the purified run at time t gives the paper definition. No absolute overlap replaces the inner product.

premises: Γ entrywise nonnegative; v coordinatewise nonnegative; finite workspace and phase-oracle states.
reviews.rationale: The type states the first quadratic bound, with uᵢ(x)=vₓ‖ctrlProjᵢ Ψₓ‖. It does not include the subsequent ≤2 maxᵢ‖Γᵢ‖, which needs normalized v and unit states and is separate.

premises: Finite state space; unit states; the same measurement set has probability at most 1/3 on one and at least 2/3 on the other.
reviews.rationale: This proves the 2√2/3 overlap estimate, not the row’s weighted final-progress inequality; that requires separate Γ support and Perron-witness reasoning.

premises: Γ symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, nonzero and zero on same-output pairs; f total.
reviews.rationale: It proves (1/35)‖Γ‖/maxᵢ‖Γᵢ‖ ≤ Q(totalise f). The nonzero opposite-output-supported Γ entails nonconstant f and a positive coordinate maximum. Perron, progress and fixed-sequence simulation are internal proof dependencies, not assumptions.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: This equality gives the Euclidean norm of the sensitivity matrix; its 0/1 adjacency and one-bit flip characterization are separate nearby definitions/theorems.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: Uniform bs≤1225 Q² covers constants and gives an explicit absolute coefficient. The star construction and general adversary route match the paper.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: Uniform λ≤35 Q covers constants with an explicit coefficient; sensitivity graph and coordinate-mask adversary route match the paper.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: One conjunction gives both explicit bounds, 1225 Q² and 35 Q, including constants.

premises: A total Boolean function of nonzero degree.
reviews.rationale: The same degree-sized face works for every outside assignment; its parity coefficient is nonzero and some parity agreement fiber has more than half the cube and sensitive edges. This is stronger than choosing one outside restriction.

The definition recursively extends the signed block matrix to d=0. The explicit one-dimensional base and equality of its entrywise absolute value with cube adjacency are separate theorems, so this definition alone is partial for the compound row.

premises: d>0; U has cardinality greater than 2^(d−1).
reviews.rationale: Its type gives a nonzero positive-root eigenvector supported on U and the unsigned induced Rayleigh inequality. The eigenspace dimension is proved using parity involution rather than the paper’s trace argument.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: Degree≤λ² includes constants. The construction follows the face and Huang-matrix method, but the equal multiplicities use a parity involution rather than the paper’s trace argument.

premises: The current total Boolean function has nonzero degree.
reviews.rationale: It provides one degree-sized support containing a nonempty sensitive block at every input. The paper row also asserts the nonconstant restriction and disjointness of blocks over successive rounds; restriction transport and round accounting are separate declarations.

premises: A total Boolean function on a finite n-cube.
reviews.rationale: The exact bound D(totalise f)≤bs(f)deg(f) is transported through the decision-tree bridge. The pinned complexitylib proof inducts using a maximum-degree support and decreasing block sensitivity, matching the paper’s algorithmic mechanism.

premises: k=l+1; m=4^t; arbitrary input.
reviews.rationale: The type bounds only the final numerator by the denominator; proof obtains |Φ|≤1 via the normalized orthogonal product, not the paper’s intermediate integer-operation count or size statement.

The type bundles width, transform and layer cost bounds, final numerator magnitude, exact realization and explicit circuit-size bound. It does not assert that every ideal intermediate integer is represented without wraparound; the source circuit uses modular encoding, so the full paper mechanism is not stated.

premises: All |σ(h,i)|≤1; m=2^n.
reviews.rationale: Bounds each ideal integer Walsh walk after l transforms by m^l. This is one piece of the intermediate-magnitude claim, not a complete circuit-operation and size assertion.

premises: All |σ(h,i)|≤1; m=2^n; arbitrary prefix length a.
reviews.rationale: Bounds an ideal final prefix sum by a·m^l; alone it neither states all intermediate operations nor the Boolean circuit size.

premises: Every input v(offset+j) for j<2^q has magnitude at most B.
reviews.rationale: Bounds an ideal partial butterfly block by 2^q B; it does not alone establish the complete intermediate magnitude, arithmetic operation counts and final circuit size.

Definition contains all-one column, promised instances, actual transcripts at true address and outward pointers. Actual circuit evaluation is the unique consistent transcript (construction_transcript_correct). No realization premise is needed for this semantic definition.
The equivalence is for arbitrary circuit and partial function; WinsAt is defined by actual promised values and gate consistency in Statement.lean. Realization is not assumed.

Gives the paper winner/true-address equivalence for arbitrary circuit, but the corrected row also contains the output-test iff, which needs a separate realization-dependent declaration. Treat the single declaration as partial, not stronger for the whole composite row.

premises: CircuitRealises C f; this is the paper’s specified realizing circuit premise.
reviews.rationale: States the corrected output-test equivalence under realization. The row separately asserts equivalence with winner plus true address, proved by construction_winsAt_iff_winner_and_address; this declaration alone is partial for the compound row.

premises: CircuitRealises C f, supplied for the construction.
reviews.rationale: Winner has some all-passing address and every address of a nonwinner has a failing test, generalized to arbitrary partial functions, circuits, inputs and dimensions. Local-test equality uses circuit realization.

premises: t >= 1; C realizes P k t; C.size <= A*mValue t*(2*t)^2 for a size constant A fixed with k.
reviews.rationale: Contains exact count and size, winning-test equivalence, adaptive depth, fixed-(i,s) coherent superposed test-index evaluation and compiled physical query bound. Corrected lem-2.2.i additionally asserts every pointer/target physical coordinate is essential; this conclusion is not in this declaration. construction_pointer_every_physical_coordinate covers it separately. Thus the prior stronger whole-conjunction tie is not warranted by this declaration alone.

premises: 1 <= k and t; 0 < ε <= 1; repetition count n at least the prescribed value; a WinsAt witness; j ≠ i.
reviews.rationale: The inequality is pointwise in arbitrary raw x and does not assume anything about the opponent’s promise. Existing source defines cmpProb from the actual comparison algorithm; the chosen n is the paper decoder repetition schedule.

premises: Actual transcript has strictly positive joint mass; independent nonnegative priors for probability interpretation.
reviews.rationale: The actual adaptive prefix factors as a schedule constraint and per-instance rectangle by classical_prefix_iff. The conclusion normalizes that rectangle into a product of classicalLaw of restricted weights. Algebra accepts real weights; probability requires nonnegativity.

premises: Nonnegative prior weights; queried instance has one unit of remaining budget; q is the next query when applying to a run.
reviews.rationale: Proves the conditional expected value inequality for the queried factor. It does not itself assert other factors unchanged, which is separately stated by classicalTranscriptValue_unchanged. Hence partial for the compound ledger row.

premises: j ≠ h; the appended query is to instance h.
reviews.rationale: Proves each other instance’s continuation value unchanged after the query. The row also explicitly mentions conditional laws and budgets and the queried-factor inequality; these are separate definitions/components, so this declaration alone is partial.

premises: Nonnegative per-instance weights; leaf output vector s; positive transcript masses when interpreting normalized laws as conditional probabilities.
reviews.rationale: The conclusion contains both product inequalities: correctness of a fixed vector at the leaf is bounded by the product of the best constant guesses, itself by the product of continuation values. For an actual positive transcript instantiate ν with transcript-restricted weights, c with remaining caps, and use product law.

premises: Nonnegative normalized address prior; no zero seen in the selected column; positive dummy transcript mass.
reviews.rationale: The exact ratio conditions on an actual adaptive transcript prefix and assigns 1/card(unqueriedRows) to each unqueried position, zero elsewhere. Prefix definitions include the schedule and the returned answers; repeated queries remove a row only once.

premises: μ nonnegative, normalized and supported on the promise; each depth-L one-instance tree succeeds with probability at most 2/3.
reviews.rationale: The event reachedCellAt includes nonheaviness of the full dummy path and a true-address cell query at zero-based t. Nested averages are original independent address and uniform zero-position laws. No hardness claim after conditioning on nonheaviness is used.

premises: L >= 1; μ nonnegative, normalized and promise-supported; depth-L one-input hardness; T.depth <= G.
reviews.rationale: The conclusion is the average original-law cellVisit event bounded by G/(mL)+G(2/3)^r with m=2^ℓ. coupledAvg samples an independent uniformly chosen I. The event is an unsplit cell encounter, not a conditional distribution.

premises: k >= 1 fixed; m=4^t and actual floored L and G as t varies.
reviews.rationale: Contains the inequality against the exact logarithmic envelope and convergence of the left-hand tail. The displayed row literally also asserts the envelope is o(1); this is the separate classical_tail_envelope_tendsto, so this declaration by itself is partial for the complete row.

premises: CircuitRealises C f, supplied by the construction.
reviews.rationale: Proves exact all-input semantic win/local-test equivalence and common adaptive depth max(3,ℓ+1). Corrected row additionally requires physical-coordinate essentiality; the separate construction_pointer_every_physical_coordinate states it.

For each chosen physical pointer or target coordinate supplies two full BitLoc inputs agreeing away from that coordinate but with differing local-test outputs. This is the essential-support clause only, not the win-equivalence and evaluation-depth clauses.

Supplies coherent retained-workspace exact evaluation of arbitrary superpositions over a common test-index type for each fixed (i,s), at logical read cap max(3,ℓ+1). Physical bit-query compilation of those witnesses requires the separate construction_controlled_compile or construction_lemma_2_2_complete.

premises: t >= 1; C realizes P k t; C.size <= A*mValue t*(2*t)^2 with A fixed for k.
reviews.rationale: The theorem includes each fixed-candidate arbitrary test-index superposition, zero wrong output amplitude and physical compiler continuation with explicit 2(2t+1) query cap, beyond the coherent big-O claim in this individual row. It also contains the test count. Its lack of physical-coordinate support matters for the separate lem-2.2.i and combined lem-2.2 rows, not this row.
Gvalue is natural division; the theorem equates it with the floor of mL/100. The corrected row is the definition only, with the lower bound in Proposition 4.2.

premises: Normalized nonnegative μ for probability interpretation.
reviews.rationale: The functional draws iid address strings and independent uniform zero positions, then applies dummy, whose X columns have one zero and whose cells are all false; this is one fixed blank pattern.

premises: The random index I is independent uniform.
reviews.rationale: The functional applies planted with independent I, but its transcript chooser tr is arbitrary and its type does not ensure correct circuit transcripts. A correct transcript chooser specializes the definition; correctness is supplied separately.

premises: Correct circuit transcript chooser; μ supported on promised inputs; sampled A has nonzero product weight.
reviews.rationale: The generic addressedF theorem proves both values on the product support. Its type does not explicitly specialize to the concrete Fkm and canonical circuit in the row.
It is the finite-set cardinality of columns whose unique zero is in the complete dummy path; repeated visits do not increment the count.
The predicate requires more than L target-address queries in the complete path; aQueries uses list countP and hence charges repeats.

premises: 1≤L; length of the fixed query path is at most G.
reviews.rationale: The bound is uniform in every fixed path and independent uniform I, so averaging over the random dummy run gives the row.

The simTree definition reads target queries up to L, answers other queries from outside data, stops before the proposed query and returns its cell address or the all-false default. Its index t is zero-based, corresponding to the paper’s t+1.

premises: 1≤L≤m; G≤mL/100; m=4^t and r=40t.
reviews.rationale: The conjunction gives all three component estimates, their sum and the strict 6/100<1/3 inequality, allowing real L and G.

premises: Fixed k≥2; C realizes P.
reviews.rationale: The theorem gives explicit 1/400, a k-dependent eventual threshold and one bound uniform in every realizing circuit. This implies the row’s fixed-k Ω estimate.

premises: k≥2; t≥8 and m=4^t.
reviews.rationale: The exact type bounds Gvalue below by 1/400 times the displayed expression. Both coefficient and threshold are uniform in k; the row only asks for an eventual positive c_k.
The type supplies one fixed circuit family, a positive constant, explicit b_k=6, the eventual quotient bound, and divergence of both lower envelope and quotient.
The type excludes every α<4 and chooses k internally, but takes R and Q reindexing plus FamilyBounds as explicit binders. Their proofs elsewhere do not remove them from this declaration.
Shows log₂(mValue t)=2t on powers of four. It does not state the global prose convention or the separate T, r, ℓ and L definitions.
Shows log₂m=2t and ceil(20 log₂m)=40t together; this says nothing by itself about T and L or the global prose convention.
Tval m is Nat.clog base 2 of 1000m, with the corresponding epsilon. The other pinned uses and global prose convention are absent.
Lvalue uses Real.logb 2 explicitly. This definition does not state the other logarithmic conventions.

constructionPartial D f is some(f x) on D and none outside; arbitrary Correct x b expresses any algorithm-specific success or error criterion. The displayed equivalence quantifies correctness only on D, with no off-domain condition. Reverse representation of arbitrary Option Bool functions is supplied by constructionPartial_reconstruct.
Every Option Bool partial function is recovered from its promise and chosen values; this declaration does not state correctness of an algorithm on its domain.
The domain of the construction is exactly D; no algorithm-correctness condition is stated.
Gives domain-only bounded-error randomized correctness with a whole-program depth bound; the row is generic over the kind and stated error of algorithm.

premises: Finite input coordinate type.
reviews.rationale: Gives domain-only quantum 2/3 correctness with normalized initial state and branch cap, plus the constant-on-promise branch; the row is generic over algorithms and stated error.

The transcript is Fin C.size→Bool, one proposed bit per non-input gate, including both output indices. Statement.lean predecessorValue reads an input predecessor from x and an earlier gate predecessor from tr; the type expands all gate consistency equations.
For m=mValue t=4^t it jointly proves log₂m=2t and ceil(20 log₂m)=40t, exactly the ℓ and r parameters of Fkm; works also at t=0.

The definitional equality exposes X, unrestricted A, pointer-bit and transcript coordinate summands. The row additionally requires the fixed bijection from ℓ-bit strings to destinations; this type itself does not mention pointerEquiv or assert its bijectivity. Specializing ℓ=2t and κ=ForrelationCoord k t gives the row’s sizes.
pointerEquiv is a bijection and each destination has a unique ℓ-bit encoding. The full X, A and cell layout is not in this type.
Gives counts m, km and 2^r at ℓ=2t and r=40t; the contents and pointer encoding of the cells are not in this type.

For tr : Fin C.size→Bool, all local gate equations hold iff tr equals the actual topological circuit evaluation. GateConsistent and predecessorValue use actual input bits and one coordinate per non-input gate, with output gates among these coordinates.

premises: Every partial-function instance in the chosen column is promised.
reviews.rationale: For an arbitrary partial function, circuit and address s, the vector of all some values equals s iff s is trueAddress; only this column is required promised, extending the specified P and circuit.

The exposed definition quantifies all j≠i and reads false at pointerEquiv applied to the ℓ pointer bits. It states the condition at any address, including the paper’s true address; it does not assert that every input satisfies the condition.

The Boolean-valued total function is true iff some i,s satisfies WinsAt. Fkm specializes addressedF to P, ℓ=2t and r=40t; winsAt_iff_paperWinsAt matches the winner predicate. Other inputs therefore produce false, not undefined.
Exact cardinality 2^ℓ+(2^ℓ−1)+r(S+2) holds generally, specializing to the displayed count. The asymptotic bound is absent.
The cardinality is exactly m+(m−1)+40t(S+2); this declaration alone does not give the asymptotic bound.

premises: t≥1; S≤A mValue(t)(2t)².
reviews.rationale: Gives explicit cubic logarithmic bound conditional on a circuit-size estimate. It does not itself state the exact count in its conclusion.

premises: k≥1; t≥1 for each circuit.
reviews.rationale: One k-dependent B bounds cardinality for an actual realizing Forrelation circuit for each t; the exact count is not in this type.

Unfolding both predicates gives exactly the all-one, promised values and true address, true transcripts and outward zero clauses. It holds for arbitrary f and C without the realizing-circuit assumption of the row, since WinsAt directly names f. Taking ∃s gives the column winner characterization; the separate local-output-test bridge does require CircuitRealises.

Pins iterationBound, trialCount and amplify=attempts at those parameters. The point-mass/uniform mixture and the stop/restart recursion are definitions and separate theorems, not explicit clauses of this type.
Gives the nonnegative normalized law with half mass on zero plus half uniform on Fin M. The particular M, trial count and stopping recursion are not stated in this type.

Each recursive trial mixes Grover lengths, restarts, runs the circuit and measures, stopping on success. Its type does not include the explicit parameter values or normalisation of the mixture. Restart is an abstract state-semantics operation, not an AdaptiveProgram compilation.

premises: 0 < A.prob < 1; H is a complex inner-product space and A is a Preparation.
reviews.rationale: Gives the normalized good/bad decomposition, angle range, all-iteration sinusoidal state and phase-equivalent normalized good component when nonzero. It additionally states orthogonality and the successful-subspace equations. A zero-probability success branch has no conditional state.

premises: γ≤A.prob≤1/2; A is a Preparation.
reviews.rationale: The theorem states both sin(2θ)=2√(p(1−p)) and √γ≤sin(2θ). Preparation supplies 0≤p≤1.

premises: γ>0 and γ≤A.prob≤1/2; A is a Preparation.
reviews.rationale: With M=iterationBound γ=ceil(10/√γ), the conjunction gives both the lower bound for the mean and 9/20 lower bound for its middle term. The proof establishes the required positive denominator.

premises: 0<γ≤1/2; 0<η<1/2; arbitrary complex inner-product space and Preparation.
reviews.rationale: One Proc amplify γ η is fixed before A and has syntactic all-branch call cap ≤138(√γ)⁻¹ log(1/η). Its phase-invariant state payoff law, zero wrong-state mass, conditional good-state law when success mass is nonzero, failure ≤η for p≥γ, and failure=1 for p=0 cover the row in the abstract Proc semantics. Proc.restart resets the branch vector; this theorem does not itself compile that semantics into the physical bit-query model or identify the output subsystem of the separate label-law implementation.
Constructs one retained-workspace circuit and complementary output labels for the two ordered probabilities. The diagonal zero clause is a separate declaration.

premises: i ≠ j.
reviews.rationale: Gives the complementarity equation on arbitrary input; self-zero is a separate declaration.

premises: Paper uses m ≥ 2; theorem is general.
reviews.rationale: Defines T with the integer base-two ceiling logarithm and ε as its reciprocal formula.
Definitionally equates Dominant with the displayed all-distinct-opponent condition.
Recursive finite expectation starts at the history L, takes weight/total normalized pivots and leaves the state unchanged at total zero; use L=[] for paper initialization.
Recursive definition starts every weight at one and appends a pivot by multiplication with a i p.

premises: Comparisons are complementary and unit valued.
reviews.rationale: Directly bounds expected total weight after T steps from the empty history by card ι / 2^T, including the zero absorbing case.

premises: Comparison values in [0,1], dominant candidate, 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and T ε < 1/2, candidate absent from history of length ≤ T.
reviews.rationale: States the full power, Bernoulli, half and positive-total chain.

premises: Comparison and unit-valued laws; dominant candidate; 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and T ε < 1/2.
reviews.rationale: Contains both inequalities of the exact absent-candidate/large-weight chain.
